tools.name: bl_status
tools.description: Whether Blender is installed (path, version, and whether it is new enough) and whether the bridge's background Blender process is running (with its pid). Never starts that process. Call this first.

tools.name: bl_scene_summary
tools.description: The scene in the bridge's background Blender (started on first use with the factory scene): file, frame range, fps, units, render settings, and every object's type, transform, dimensions, parent and materials. Read-only. It is not the scene open in your Blender window.

tools.name: bl_catalog
tools.description: List the operations bl_do can run: name, effect (read/write/destructive), description and params as JSON Schema. Never starts Blender.

tools.name: bl_do
tools.description: Run one operation by name with its params in the background Blender (started on first use). Discover operations and their params with bl_catalog first. Params are checked before Blender starts.

params.description: The operation's params object (see bl_catalog). Omit when it takes none.

tools.name: bl_get_skill
tools.description: Read the bundled Xelta Blender skills (offline). Without args: the skill index. With name: that skill's SKILL.md. With name + reference: one of its reference files. Load 'xelta-bl-editing-rules' first, before working in Blender; 'xelta-bl-product-shot' for product stills and turntables; 'xelta-bl-destruction' for a destruction shot; 'xelta-bl-scene-building' for an animated scene from a prompt.

name.description: Skill name from the index, e.g. 'xelta-bl-editing-rules'.

reference.description: A reference listed for that skill, e.g. 'references/x.md' or 'x'.

tools.name: bl_preview
tools.description: See the scene through its active camera: a quick, low-sample Cycles PNG (denoised) rendered in the background Blender, a few seconds at the defaults. The longest side is max_side (default 512; never larger than the scene's own render); a JSON summary {width, height, engine, seconds} follows the image. It does not change the scene or its render settings. NO_CAMERA when the scene has no camera. Use it to check framing, materials and lighting before a final render with render.still.

max_side.description: Longest side in pixels, an integer from 64 to 1024 (default 512).

samples.description: Cycles samples, an integer from 1 to 64 (default 16).

tools.name: bl_job_status
tools.description: A render or bake job's state: queued, running, done, failed or cancelled, with progress {frame, total}, output, engine, started_at, finished_at, error (RENDER_FAILED or BAKE_FAILED with the job's last log lines) and warnings (e.g. ENGINE_FALLBACK). With id, that job; without, every job of this server session, newest first. Never starts Blender. JOB_NOT_FOUND for an unknown id.

id.description: The job id render.still, render.turntable or sim.bake returned.

tools.name: bl_job_cancel
tools.description: Stop a queued or running render job: its Blender is killed, it becomes cancelled, and nothing is written at its output path (a cancelled sim.bake leaves the saved .blend unbaked). A finished job is returned unchanged. The next queued job starts. JOB_NOT_FOUND for an unknown id.

id.description: The job id render.still, render.turntable or sim.bake returned.

tools.name: bl_python
tools.description: Runs a Python script inside the bridge's own background Blender (best-effort write guard, not a sandbox; needs the user's yes). It is the scene process, not the user's open Blender, with `bpy` available: an escape hatch for one-off effects no typed operation covers, so prefer the typed operations (bl_catalog, bl_do). It needs the user's explicit yes: show them the script, then pass confirm: true; anything else is INVALID_ARGS and nothing runs. While it runs, the guard refuses writes outside write_roots (absolute folders the user approved, 0-8) and the bridge's runtime dir, and the common process-launch and network routes (GUARD_BLOCKED); reads are not guarded. The guard is best effort and not a sandbox: Image.save(), bpy.data.libraries.write(), real bpy via sys.modules, compositor outputs and C-level exporters reached by other routes are not caught. Returns {stdout, stderr (last 200 lines each), value (the script's `result` variable, JSON-safe), guard: 'best-effort', readback}; the scene is marked changed after every run. A raised exception is PYTHON_ERROR with the traceback; past timeout_s (1-600, default 60) Blender is stopped (TIMEOUT) and the scene is lost; threads left running (THREADS_LEFT_RUNNING) also restart it. BAKE_IN_PROGRESS while a bake job writes the scene's file, or for a save or open of a file being baked; UNSAVED_CHANGES for a file reload over unsaved changes.

script.description: Python source, a string of 1 B to 100 KB. `bpy` is predefined; set a variable `result` to return a value.

confirm.description: Must be the boolean true, and only after the user explicitly agreed to run it.

write_roots.description: Absolute folders the user approved for writes, an array of 0-8 strings (default none).

timeout_s.description: Seconds before Blender is stopped, a number from 1 to 600 (default 60).
